given.part: An open loan's `dueOn` is before today

breaks.break: Loans are never picked up as overdue, or only some are
A loan due today is treated as overdue (`<=`)
A returned loan is treated as open

given.why: Loans due 03-16 are sent on 03-17. B2's test covers the due-today boundary and the returned case.

breaks.break: Today is taken in local time rather than UTC
Today is taken from a date other than the clock's UTC date

given.why: The clock is always 10:00Z, so local time and UTC give the same date in nearly every zone. No test sits near a UTC midnight boundary.

given.part: it has no reminder recorded today

breaks.break: A reminder recorded on an earlier day also blocks sending
A loan with no reminder at all is skipped

given.why: No test has a reminder from a previous day that should still allow a send today. B2 only covers a reminder from today.

breaks.break: The API is never called, for example a dry run

then.why: fakeNotifications.sent must have exactly 2 entries.

breaks.break: The wrong id (loanId) is sent as memberId
Members are mixed up between loans

then.why: Each sent entry is matched on memberId, loanId and dueOn, with distinct members.

breaks.break: No reminder row is written

then.why: The reminders table is read and must have 2 rows.

breaks.break: sent_on is set to dueOn
sent_on is set to the wrong day

then.why: sent_on must equal 2026-03-17, which differs from dueOn 03-16.

breaks.break: The reminder is recorded before the API is asked

then.why: The row doesn't state ordering; per mutants.json it only shows on refusal, which B3 covers.

given.part: An open loan already has a reminder recorded today

Reminder lookup compares the wrong day

breaks.break: A returned loan is still reminded

given.why: loan2 is overdue and returned, and only loan1 is expected to be sent.

Any not-yet-due loan is reminded

given.why: loan3 is due exactly on today, which is the boundary case, and it must not be sent.

breaks.break: Any of the three skipped cases is still sent
Nothing at all is sent, including the legitimate loan

then.why: sent must match exactly [{loanId: loan1}], so extra sends fail and a missing loan1 fails.

breaks.break: Only 200 is accepted
Only 200/202 is accepted
A 2xx other than 200, 202 or 204 (for example 201 or 299) is refused

then.why: 200, 202 and 204 are tested. A hard-coded list of those three would pass, and no other 2xx is tested.

breaks.break: Only 5xx is refused
3xx or 1xx answers are accepted

then.why: Only a 400 is tested. Redirects and other non-2xx classes are not.

breaks.break: The network error is thrown rather than turned into a refusal
A failed connection is treated as accepted

then.why: HttpResponse.error() must produce a refused result.
